items.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: I would go to the Kentucky Club and see Jackie Wilson and all those artists, those rhythm & blues artists that were coming through then at that time

ctx.x: You’ve played some traditional jazz along the way early on?

Um hum. My first gig out of college. This was one of the things that started making me like the instrument. My first gig was on — not really first gig, my first gig on tuba was at a place called Your Father’s Moustache. There was a whole chain of these things in Philadelphia and New York, St. Louis, Chicago, Joel Schiavone, his father was like this scrap metal millionaire you know. And Joel his son, with his play money I guess, established these clubs. And they did well for quite a while so they opened one in…

Father’s Moustache. And I got so good at it that they hired me this next summer, this was like ’67, the summer of ’67, to go down to Summer’s Point and work at a club in Summer’s Point. So I lived in Atlantic City and I would go to the Kentucky Club and see Jackie Wilson and all those artists, those rhythm & blues artists that were coming through then at that time, and then I would work over at Summer’s Point at My Father’s Moustache during that whole summer. It was a great summer.
